overall_reason: The demo shows a 'Link copied' toast whose dismiss control darkens on press at about 1.6 s before the toast leaves, which is feedback in the right order, but the demo ends on an empty frame and the exit itself falls between stills.

score.reason: T-POSTER fails because the end state is an empty stage; T-CONTINUITY passes for the press before the result, and T-ENTER-EXIT could not be judged from the stills.

findings.where: div.tc-exit toast demo, final frame and fold-1440.png
findings.evidence: fold-1440.png has no pixel darker than 250 anywhere, and the stills from about 2.6 s to 5.5 s show an empty white stage. The demo holds nothing after the toast leaves.
findings.before: The demo ends on a blank stage for more than 3 s
findings.after: Hold a payoff after the dismiss (the content the toast sat over, or the toast's resting place) and use that as the poster frame
findings.why: A thumbnail, a reduced-motion viewer or a screenshot of this demo shows nothing, so it cannot say what the dismiss does.

strengths: The dismiss control shows a pressed background, rgb(234, 234, 234), at about 1.6 s while the toast is still whole, so the press reads before the result.
not_investigated: T-ENTER-EXIT: the toast's exit (the stylesheet declares opacity and a 4 px rise over 320 ms on .tc-toast[data-leaving]) happens between the 1.6 s and 2.6 s stills, so whether this toast fades or vanishes in one frame is not visible.
Frame-level timing: the passive stills are seven shots over 6 s from a separate load, so durations and curves come from the declarations at 1440, not from frames between stills.
Sweep motion (MOT-002) is not-verified: motion capture was skipped (--no-motion) and there were no click runs; async_state (CMP-001) is not-verified (--no-async).
T-RAPID-TOGGLE and interruptibility: no detector built and no click runs.
Gestures and drags as a person plays them, scroll-driven motion, hover as it plays (only declarations read), and route or page transitions: not captured.
The shared stylesheet's 8 motion_css (MOT-001) hits belong to the sweep and are not repeated here.
